title: Urban beekeeping
script: Narrator: In recent years, beekeeping has become popular in large cities such as London and Tokyo. Many companies have placed beehives on the roofs of their office buildings, partly to show that they care about the environment. However, some scientists warn that this trend may cause problems. Honeybees compete with wild bees for flowers, and in cities there are often not enough flowers to support large numbers of bees. As a result, wild bee populations may decline. Experts say that instead of adding more beehives, cities should focus on planting more flowers and trees that provide food for all kinds of pollinating insects.
translation: 近年、ロンドンや東京などの大都市で養蜂が人気になっている。多くの企業が、環境への配慮を示すこともあって、オフィスビルの屋上に巣箱を設置している。しかし、一部の科学者はこの流行が問題を引き起こすかもしれないと警告している。ミツバチは花をめぐって野生のハチと競合し、都市には多くのハチを支えるだけの花がないことが多い。その結果、野生のハチの数が減るおそれがある。専門家は、巣箱を増やすよりも、あらゆる受粉昆虫のえさとなる花や木を増やすことに都市は力を入れるべきだと述べている。

questions.question: Why do some companies keep bees on their roofs?
choices: To show their concern for the environment.
To sell honey to their employees.
To help scientists with their research.
To reduce the number of wild bees.
questions.explanation: partly to show that they care about the environment と述べられている。

questions.question: What do experts recommend?
choices: Planting more flowers and trees in cities.
Banning beekeeping in large cities.
Moving beehives to the countryside.
Increasing the number of honeybees.
questions.explanation: 巣箱を増やすより花や木を植えることに力を入れるべきだと勧めている。

title: Sleep and memory
script: Narrator: Scientists have long known that sleep is important for health, but recent research suggests that it also plays a key role in learning. During deep sleep, the brain appears to replay information that was learned during the day. This process helps move memories from short-term storage to long-term storage. In one experiment, students who slept after studying a list of words remembered more of them the next day than students who stayed awake. Researchers say this means that staying up all night to study before an exam may actually be less effective than getting a good night's sleep.
translation: 科学者は以前から睡眠が健康に重要だと知っていたが、最近の研究では学習においても重要な役割を果たすことが示されている。深い眠りの間、脳はその日に学んだ情報を再生しているようだ。この過程は、記憶を短期の保存から長期の保存に移すのを助ける。ある実験では、単語リストを勉強した後に眠った学生は、起きていた学生よりも翌日多くの単語を覚えていた。研究者によると、これは試験前に徹夜で勉強するのは、ぐっすり眠るより実は効果が低いかもしれないことを意味するという。

questions.question: What does the brain seem to do during deep sleep?
choices: Delete unnecessary memories.
Create new dreams from old memories.
Rest completely without any activity.
Replay information learned during the day.
questions.explanation: 深い眠りの間、日中に学んだ情報を再生しているようだと述べられている。

questions.question: What do researchers suggest about studying before exams?
choices: Students should study in the early morning.
Studying with friends improves memory.
Sleeping well may be better than studying all night.
Short naps are better than long sleep.
questions.explanation: 徹夜で勉強するより、ぐっすり眠るほうが効果的かもしれないと述べている。

title: Night-shift workers' health
script: Narrator: Millions of people around the world work night shifts in jobs such as nursing, security, and manufacturing. Research has shown that working at night for many years may increase the risk of health problems, including heart disease and diabetes. One reason is that night work disrupts the body's internal clock, which controls when we feel sleepy and how our bodies process food. Experts recommend that night-shift workers keep a regular sleep schedule, even on their days off, and avoid eating large meals in the middle of the night. Some companies are also designing shift schedules that rotate forward, from morning to evening to night, which is easier for the body to adjust to.
translation: 世界中で何百万人もの人々が、看護や警備、製造業などの仕事で夜勤をしている。研究によると、長年夜間に働くと、心臓病や糖尿病などの健康問題のリスクが高まる可能性がある。理由の一つは、夜勤が体内時計を乱すことだ。体内時計は、いつ眠くなるか、体が食べ物をどう処理するかを制御している。専門家は、夜勤の人は休日でも規則正しい睡眠スケジュールを守り、真夜中に大量の食事をとるのを避けるよう勧めている。また、朝から夕方、夜へと順方向に回るシフトを設計している企業もある。そのほうが体が適応しやすいからだ。

questions.question: What is one reason night work may cause health problems?
choices: Night workers usually earn less money.
It disrupts the body's internal clock.
Night workers rarely exercise.
It is more physically demanding.
questions.explanation: 夜勤が体内時計(internal clock)を乱すことが理由の一つ。

questions.question: What do experts recommend for night-shift workers?
choices: Keeping a regular sleep schedule.
Eating a large meal at midnight.
Changing shifts as often as possible.
Sleeping only on their days off.
questions.explanation: 休日でも規則正しい睡眠スケジュールを守るよう勧めている。

title: Coral reef restoration
script: Narrator: Coral reefs are home to about a quarter of all marine species, but they are being damaged by rising ocean temperatures. When the water becomes too warm, corals lose the tiny algae that live inside them and give them color. This process, known as coral bleaching, can kill large areas of reef. Scientists are now trying to help reefs recover by growing small pieces of coral in underwater nurseries and then planting them on damaged reefs. Some researchers are also breeding corals that can survive in warmer water. However, they warn that these methods cannot save reefs unless global warming itself is slowed down.
translation: サンゴ礁には全海洋生物種の約4分の1が生息しているが、海水温の上昇によって被害を受けている。水温が高くなりすぎると、サンゴは体内にすんで色を与えている小さな藻類を失う。白化と呼ばれるこの現象によって、広い範囲のサンゴ礁が死ぬことがある。現在、科学者は海中の育成場で小さなサンゴのかけらを育て、それを被害を受けたサンゴ礁に植えることで回復を助けようとしている。より温かい水でも生き延びられるサンゴを育種している研究者もいる。しかし彼らは、地球温暖化そのものを遅らせない限り、こうした方法ではサンゴ礁を救えないと警告している。

questions.question: What causes coral bleaching?
choices: Pollution from ships.
Fishing with nets.
Water that is too warm.
A lack of sunlight.
questions.explanation: 水温が高くなりすぎるとサンゴが藻類を失い白化する。

questions.question: What do the scientists warn?
choices: Underwater nurseries harm fish.
Coral breeding is too expensive.
Global warming must be slowed to save reefs.
Reefs will recover on their own.
questions.explanation: 地球温暖化を遅らせない限り救えないと警告している。

title: Standing desks
script: Narrator: Many office workers sit for more than eight hours a day, and studies have linked long periods of sitting to health problems such as back pain and weight gain. As a result, standing desks have become popular in offices. These desks can be raised so that people can work while standing. However, researchers say that standing all day is not the answer either, because it can cause problems with the legs and feet. Instead, they recommend changing positions regularly, for example, by standing for a while every thirty minutes. Taking short walks during the day is also an effective way to reduce the risks of sitting too long.
translation: 多くの会社員は1日8時間以上座っており、研究では長時間座ることが腰痛や体重増加などの健康問題と関連づけられている。その結果、オフィスでスタンディングデスクが人気になっている。こうした机は高さを上げられ、立ったまま仕事ができる。しかし研究者によると、一日中立っているのも答えではない。脚や足に問題を起こすことがあるからだ。代わりに、例えば30分ごとにしばらく立つなど、定期的に姿勢を変えることを勧めている。日中に短い散歩をすることも、座りすぎのリスクを減らす効果的な方法である。

questions.question: What do researchers say about standing all day?
choices: It is the best way to work.
It helps people lose weight quickly.
It can also cause health problems.
It improves concentration.
questions.explanation: 一日中立つのも脚や足に問題を起こすことがあると述べている。

questions.question: What do researchers recommend?
choices: Changing positions regularly.
Sitting for no more than four hours.
Using a standing desk all day.
Exercising before work.
questions.explanation: 定期的に姿勢を変えることを勧めている。
